slides.title: Roles
slides.html: Each phone has one role, picked on Your role the first time Drones opens. From then on Drones shows only that role's pages.

slides.title: Forward observer officer (FOO)
slides.html: The FOO asks for drones and follows each mission. My requests shows where each request stands, such as Waiting for the HQ.

slides.title: HQ
slides.html: The HQ gives waiting requests to drone teams with Assign. It draws corridors, the areas where teams may fly, and alone gives quotas, a set number of requests a day.

slides.title: TOC
slides.html: A TOC, a platoon's tactical operations centre, works like the HQ for its own teams. It gives them requests with Assign and draws their corridors, but gives no quotas.

slides.title: Drone team
slides.html: The team's navigator, or crew observer, takes the Drone team role. They keep the team's drones, plan each mission, run it and report how it went.

slides.title: Pilot
slides.html: The Pilot role is for the drone team's second phone. Its one page gives the bearing and distance from drone to target, the planned height and the flight time left.

slides.title: Requests
slides.html: A request asks for a Strike or a Recon on an enemy mark or area. To says who should answer, and a request no team takes lapses after two hours.

slides.title: Corridors
slides.html: A corridor is the area where a team may fly, for set hours. It shows shaded on the map, and a plan warns when its route leaves it.

slides.title: Quotas
slides.html: A quota gives a forward observer, or a whole unit, a number of requests a day to one team. The Request sheet then lists that team first under To.

slides.title: Missions and plans
slides.html: A mission is one drone flight on a request, such as Strike 1. Its plan flags problems with Range, and with Weather when Weather lookups is on, but the team decides.

slides.title: Drone types
slides.html: A drone team lists its drones by type, with range, flight time and how many it has. Plans use these limits, and the HQ and TOC see them.

slides.title: What everyone sees
slides.html: Phones on the drone feeds show corridors, routes, drones and the circle around each target, even without OpenDefence UAVOps. In OpenDefence UAVOps, Watch on a flying mission opens its video.

slides.title: A plugin on OpenDefence Main
slides.html: OpenDefence UAVOps is a separate plugin that works through OpenDefence Main's Request sheet and Inbox. When an admin sets Quotas and corridors to Off there, requests go straight to the teams.
